sections.html: Synodontis frontosus Vaillant, 1895. Type locality: White Nile River, Sudan. Maximum size: 342 mm (13.5") SL. IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2019).
Africa: Nile basin, Lakes Rudolf, Albert, Edward and Kyoga; Chad basin; and Uebi Giuba (Uebi Shebeli).
Feeds on algae, macrophytes, detritus, crustaceans, insects and mollusks.

Lay the fish in your hand with its head toward your palm and the tail toward your fingers. Hold the dorsal spine between your middle and ring finger so the fish is belly up; the sharp fin spines can puncture the hand, so be careful. The genital pore is in a small furrow of tissue (in healthy fish) and is obstructed by the pelvic fins. Pull down on the tail gently to arch the spine; the pelvic fins stand and the furrow opens to display the genital pore and the anus.

The male has a somewhat ridged genital papilla on which the spermatoduct is on the back side, facing the tail fin. A gravid female also shows an extended papilla, but the oviduct is on the ventral side of the papilla. It may show a little redness if really gravid. A thin or emaciated female will have just two pink pores, the oviduct and the anus.
Unreported. Breeding takes place during flooding in June to early dry down in January. There is no breeding report.

All species in the genus Synodontis have a hardened head cap with a humeral process behind the gill opening, pointed towards the posterior. The dorsal and pectoral fins have a hardened, serrated first ray. The caudal fin is always forked. There is one pair of maxillary barbels, sometimes with membranes and occasionally branched. The two pairs of mandibular barbels are often branched and can have nodes. The cone-shaped teeth in the upper jaw are short; those in the lower jaw are S-shaped and movable. These fish produce audible sounds when disturbed by rubbing the base of the pectoral spine against the pectoral girdle.

Etymology: according to Cuvier, Synodontis is an "ancient name for an undetermined fish from the Nile".
Bulletin de la Société Philomathique de Paris (Sér. 8) v. 7 (no. 16) (for 8 June 1895), pp 48.
